_readme: Public figures encoded into the childhood-brain schema from published biographies. consent=public means: no private data, only facts the person has stated on record or that appear in mainstream published biographies. Every judgment call is labeled in `labels` with evidence and a confidence (high/med/low). `outcome` is the adult ground truth and must NEVER be passed to a brain; evals/outcomes.ts keeps it hidden. Seed slugs come from evals/brains/prototype-data.ts; preference/fear/stress values come from the closed tables in evals/data/derive.ts, chosen by the labeler to best fit the documented adult, not derived mechanically from the picks.

people.name: Elon
sources: Maye Musk, A Woman Makes a Plan (2019); Walter Isaacson, Elon Musk (2023)

parent1.evidence: Errol Musk: engineer, wealthy, but Elon and Maye both describe belittling, hours-long lectures, and abuse; Elon calls him 'a terrible human being'. Moods set the weather of the house.

parent2.evidence: Maye Musk after the 1979 divorce: multiple jobs, frugal, sacrificed for three kids; Elon lived mostly with Errol from ~10, so Maye's love arrived as sacrifice at a distance.

school.evidence: Waterkloof House Preparatory, Bryanston High, then Pretoria Boys High School, an elite boys' school. Isaacson describes the money-and-status culture.

event1.evidence: Parents divorced 1979 when he was eight; the house had a before and an after.

event2.evidence: Bullied for years; at ~12 thrown down concrete stairs and hospitalized.

event3.evidence: Read the encyclopedia, then taught himself to code; wrote and sold the game Blastar at 12.

event4.evidence: At 17 left South Africa for Canada against his father's wishes and to avoid conscription.

comfort.evidence: Retreats into books, engineering, work; the things nobody gave him.

way_of_loving.evidence: Describes care mostly as providing and building for people; many children, funds, projects.

core_fear.evidence: Closest closed-set value to a child of a volatile father; his stated fears (civilizational collapse) are not in the vocabulary.

social_fear.evidence: Documented compulsion to answer doubters and short-sellers; bullied kid who now cannot let 'they said it was impossible' stand.

under_stress.evidence: Works more: factory floor, 100-hour weeks, sleeping at the plant during Model 3 ramp.

under_conflict.evidence: Escalates publicly and treats every fight as a contest to win (SEC, journalists, unions, Twitter).

outcome.summary: Co-founded Zip2, X.com/PayPal, SpaceX, Tesla (CEO), Neuralink, The Boring Company, xAI; bought Twitter. Repeatedly the richest person alive.

facts.value: turns it into a test to win
My father could talk at us for hours and we were not allowed to leave the room. I learned to read the house before I learned to read the room.
The older boys threw me down the concrete stairs and I woke up in hospital. School was a place to survive and books were the way out.
My parents split when I was eight. I chose to live with my father because he seemed alone. I have said since that it was a mistake.
At twelve I wrote a space game called Blastar and a magazine paid me five hundred dollars for it. It was the first thing that was entirely mine.

people.name: Sam
sources: Tad Friend, 'Sam Altman's Manifest Destiny', The New Yorker (2016)

parent1.evidence: Connie Gibstine, dermatologist; steady, accepting ('I always thought of him as just sort of unisexual and tech-y'). Feelings had a place to land.

parent2.evidence: Jerry Altman, real estate broker, remembered for helping anyone who asked; present and ordinary.

school.evidence: John Burroughs School, a private prep school in St. Louis.

event1.evidence: Got a Macintosh at eight, took it apart, learned to program.

event2.evidence: At 17 came out to the whole school in an assembly speech after a Christian group tried to boycott a sexuality assembly; standing ovation.

event3.evidence: Praised as the smart one from nursery school (grasped area codes at four).

event4.evidence: The assembly speech and the ovation: for one day the story was about him and it was good. Also Stanford admission.

comfort.evidence: Computers and building; the thing nobody gave him.

way_of_loving.evidence: Loyalty-based; stays with people and institutions (YC, OpenAI) through crises.

core_fear.evidence: Closed-set best fit for a lifelong top student who frames everything as a bet he must not lose in public.

social_fear.evidence: Elite-school pattern; repeated public concern with being seen as trustworthy or 'not consistently candid'.

under_stress.evidence: November 2023 firing: stayed calm, organized, quiet, and let others make noise.

under_conflict.evidence: Turned the board fight into a contest he won within five days.

outcome.summary: Founded Loopt at 19, president of Y Combinator, co-founded and runs OpenAI (ChatGPT); fired and reinstated as CEO in 2023.

facts.value: turns it into a test to win
My mother was a dermatologist and my father sold real estate and helped anyone who asked him. Nothing at home needed managing.
I got a Macintosh at eight and took it apart to see how it worked. Nobody gave me that and nobody could take it.
At seventeen I stood up in front of the whole school and said I was gay, after a Christian group tried to shut the assembly down. I had rewritten the speech all night in the hallway.
I was the smart one before I was anything else, the kid who understood how area codes worked in nursery school.

people.name: Mark
sources: Jose Antonio Vargas, 'The Face of Facebook', The New Yorker (2010)

parent1.evidence: Karen Kempner, psychiatrist who stopped practicing to raise four kids; steady household in Dobbs Ferry.

parent2.evidence: Edward Zuckerberg, dentist with the practice attached to the house; taught Mark Atari BASIC, said 'find what they're passionate about' rather than push. Present and ordinary rather than hero-making.

school.evidence: Ardsley High School (public) then Phillips Exeter Academy, one of the most elite boarding schools in the country.

event1.evidence: Father hired software developer David Newman to tutor him at ~11; Newman called him a prodigy and said it was hard to stay ahead of him.

event2.evidence: Coding as the private world: ZuckNet at 11-12 connecting the house to the dental office.

event3.evidence: Synapse Media Player at 17 drew acquisition interest from Microsoft and AOL; fencing team captain at Exeter.

event4.evidence: Labeled a prodigy early; the smart one across four siblings.

comfort.evidence: Coding, the private world nobody gave him.

way_of_loving.evidence: Long, steady relationships (Priscilla Chan since 2003); loyalty to early team.

core_fear.evidence: Closed-set best fit; his stated fear is irrelevance ('if we don't build the thing that kills Facebook, someone else will').

social_fear.evidence: Elite-school pattern plus well-documented discomfort in public scrutiny (2018 Senate hearings).

under_stress.evidence: Declares 'lockdown', organizes the company, goes quiet publicly.

under_conflict.evidence: Treats competitors as tests to win: copied Snapchat Stories, launched Threads against X, challenged Musk to a cage fight.

outcome.summary: Founded Facebook at 19 in a Harvard dorm; founder, chairman and CEO of Meta; one of the five richest people alive.

facts.value: turns it into a test to win
My mother was a psychiatrist and my father a dentist with the office attached to the house. Dinner happened every night and it was fine.
My father taught me Atari BASIC and then hired a programmer to tutor me. The tutor said it was hard to stay ahead of me. I was eleven.
I built a program so the computers in the house could talk to the ones in the dental office. I called it ZuckNet.
At boarding school I wrote a music player that learned what you liked. Companies offered to buy it and I said no and went to college instead.

people.name: Garry
sources: Garry Tan, own account of his father's alcoholism and the family's food scarcity (podcasts and blog)

parent1.evidence: Father: mechanical engineer from Singapore who drank heavily and changed jobs often; Garry describes an angry alcoholic who prioritized beer over groceries.

parent2.evidence: Mother from Burma: two jobs including a convalescent home, limited English kept her from becoming a nurse; everything given, nothing said.

school.evidence: Fremont, California public schools after the family settled there in 1991; specific school not verified.

event1.evidence: Periods of food scarcity: bread and milk weeks; father's unstable employment.

event2.evidence: Immigrant kid doing the forms and the English for parents with limited English.

event3.evidence: Born in Winnipeg, moved to California, back to Canada, then Fremont in 1991: the new kid more than once.

event4.evidence: Taught himself to code at 14 and cold-called the Yellow Pages for web work to help his parents buy a house.

comfort.evidence: Says he still tracks prices and money as safety.

way_of_loving.evidence: The mother's pattern; his YC identity is built on giving to founders.

core_fear.evidence: Child of an alcoholic: the mood changing without warning.

social_fear.evidence: Immigrant kid who fights being underestimated; central to his public persona.

under_stress.evidence: Hypervigilance he has discussed in the context of therapy; reads the room and the door.

under_conflict.evidence: Escalates publicly and picks winnable fights (San Francisco politics, GrowSF).

outcome.summary: Co-founded Posterous (acquired by Twitter), Initialized Capital (early Coinbase, Instacart); president and CEO of Y Combinator since 2023; prominent SF political fighter.

facts.value: turns it into a test to win
My father was a mechanical engineer who drank too much and changed jobs a lot. I learned the difference between a good night and a bad one from the sound of the door.
My mother worked two jobs, one at a convalescent home, and never got to become the nurse she wanted to be. Her English was not enough for the forms, so I did them.
Some weeks it was bread and milk. I knew what a case of beer cost before I knew what rent was.
At fourteen I taught myself to make webpages and cold-called businesses out of the Yellow Pages so my parents could buy a house.
